learning_outcomes.text: Upon completion of the course, the student will be able to specify and structure an industrial project using traditional project management tools.
She/he will also master the fundamental concepts of quality in the industry and apply statistical process control methods to ensure compliance and optimize industrial processes.
Assimilate the principles of project management and their importance in an industrial context.
Understand the evolution of quality approaches and their role in business competitiveness.
Familiarize with planning and control tools for industrial projects.
Develop and structure a project by defining its scope and priorities.
Implement planning tools such as activity networks, PERT, and GANTT.
Construct and use control charts to monitor an industrial process.
Develop a rigorous approach to project management and quality assurance.
Recognize the impact of quality on performance and customer trust.
Integrate best practices in industrial management within a professional setting.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Project Management
Definition and importance of industrial projects
Role of the project manager and project management methodologies
Project Planning and Structuring
Logical approach to project definition
Project scope and breakdown structure (PBS)
Logical dependencies and task scheduling
Project Management Tools and Resource Allocation
Use of PERT and GANTT tools
Resource planning and scheduling
Risk management and project monitoring
Definition and structuring of a project
Project development using activity networks
Project development using PERT and GANTT diagrams
Use of MS Project software for project development, resource scheduling, and project monitoring
Introduction to Quality and Its History
Definition of quality
Concepts of compliance and non-compliance
Evolution of quality concepts: quality control, quality assurance, TQM
Statistical Process Control
"Zero defect" objective and quality challenges in the industry
Statistical process control (SPC) methods
Use of control charts and capability indicators
Construction and analysis of a control chart
Application of quality tools to an industrial case
teaching_methods: Interactive lectures with visual aids, case studies, and discussions
Tutorials (TD) for practical exercises, case studies, and simulations
Practical work (TP) incorporating specialized software such as MS Project for project planning
